notes.title: FLASHOUT III Announced! Coming in 2022! Add to your wishlist!
notes.content:
[b]Hello all Jujubee fans! Today we have some great news to announce:

FLASHOUT is back and is racing into Steam this very year! [/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6106540/5c0dcc32c2114159e6b1479782654d88882756ec.gif[/img]

[h3]YEEES… FLASHOUT IS BACK![/h3]

Where high speed meets high stakes. Where unforgiving combat, loud electronic music and addictive boosts of adrenaline mix up to separate winners from losers. Where gravitation is nothing more than an empty word. This is where the world of [b]FLASHOUT 3[/b] will take you and your ride to the absolute limits!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6106540/35475072352a1c1b763332fc75947d2e4b3680d7.gif[/img]

[b]FLASHOUT 3[/b] will offer you ultra-fast ships, loops, jumps and sudden razor-sharp turns! You will have the chance to test your racing skills on the most impressive sci-fi circuits and try not to fall behind! But if it happens, don't sweat! Unleash the power of rockets, guns, bombs and mines to help you level down your competition!

[previewyoutube=NiSL2s8E9Ig;full][/previewyoutube]
In [b]FLASHOUT 3[/b] you will take part in an exciting, head-to-head fight to the finish! Witness spectacular crashes, the agony of defeat, and the sweet taste of victory! But don't blink! It can all end in a flash!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/6106540/6da6f2126bff8f236d9bfec883bca9ae3a5e39f5.gif[/img]

FLASHOUT was also always about music, so expect great and unique electronic tunes!

[b]Steam users can expect a playable demo version by the end of May! [/b]The full version of the game is coming later this year to PC (Windows, Mac, Linux)!

Make sure to wishlist the game!

[url=https://www.facebook.com/JujubeeGames]Follow JUJUBEE on Facebook[/url]

notes.title: Jujubee's New Survival-Strategy Game Is Coming! (June 2020)
notes.content:
[b][h1]HEY EVERYONE![/h1][/b]

We are just dropping by to inform everyone of our latest, upcoming title - Dark Moon. We are confident that fans of both strategy and survival games will find a lot of joy in our dark universe.

Dark Moon is a survival strategy game where in order to survive you must avoid the Sun’s scorching rays and embrace the darkness. Gather resources, upgrade your mobile base, make tough moral decisions, but most importantly - don’t go into the light!

[h1]Take a look at the Announcement Trailer[/h1]
[previewyoutube=o-25KVaVAhI;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1][b]Dark Moon's features include:[/b][/h1]
[b]SOLAR PRESSURE[/b]
The Sun is destroying everything it touches, you must avoid its radiance. The Mechaplex - a giant, general-purpose engineering vehicle will stand as your base of operations. It will also serve as your getaway vehicle, thus plan your actions accordingly and escape the tireless enemy. You must constantly move forward.

[b]NON-LINEAR SURVIVAL[/b]
A different experience with each playthrough as each location and event may bring unpredictable results. Scan the terrain and obstacles with your drones to prepare for what lies ahead. Embrace or beware of other survivors who will want to join your convoy. Gather minerals and use their properties to increase your chances of survival.

[b]MANAGE YOUR MOBILE BASE[/b]
The Mechaplex is your means of survival; build new buildings on top of it, research new technologies, enhance your crew's abilities, and traverse the lunar plains. Develop new mechanical prototypes that will enhance your mineral gathering or focus on enhancing your convoy's movement speed to elude the Sun's deadly grasp. You can't stay in one place for too long.

[h1][b]Wishlist the game:[/b][/h1]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1105330

We hope you will accompany us on this journey of returning home from the Moon and thank you for taking the time to read this short announcement. Dark Moon is coming [b]June 2020[/b]!

Cheers!

notes.title: Recreating History with Kursk - An Indie Developer’s Tribute
notes.content:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/2mwdIUq.gif[/img]

[h1][b]GREETINGS![/b][/h1]

On this day, 19 years ago, the nuclear submarine [b]K-141 Kursk[/b] sank into the Barents Sea taking the lives of all 118 personnel on board. Here at Jujubee, we would like to commemorate this tragic event by presenting a small journey of a Polish indie studio trying to recreate the past and tell the story of those brave men as accurately as possible. If you haven’t played the game we highly encourage you to do so as potential spoilers may be present in this post. Without further ado, welcome to the past, ladies and gentlemen.

Before we even set our foot on the submarine we’ve decided a short prologue would be a good starting point. And what better place to start the game then from the beautiful Moscow itself?  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/YpsVApT.gif[/img]

This scene below is quite symbolic knowing what will eventually happen in a couple of hours, so we wanted to give it the significance it deserved. The last opportunity to witness the beautiful horizon and the Russian armada heading out to perform their scheduled practice maneuvers. Please, take it in.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/TG87WrW.gif[/img]

We are quite meticulous in our approach to achieve the most realistic representation of the submarine, so here we’re showcasing one of our, let’s say, technical documents. Bringing back this vessel with all of its sections and individual rooms took a lot of work, but that’s a comfortable price to pay if you want to achieve this level of accuracy and realism. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/I6z7Plr.png[/img]

Speaking of realism, we wanted the player to have the opportunity to fully explore the vessel, so about 90% of rooms are open for the curious people out there. Rooms may seem identical (they were built this way), but we wanted to give some personal touch to the people who lived in those quarters, so a player might expect someone playing a video game whilst using a second chair to set his feet comfortably. The crew was working shifts, so the player could encounter some personnel simply resting after a tough night. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/VaMTfes.gif[/img]

We had done a lot of research on the technology that was used in early 2000 as well. Even though we remembered some bits and pieces of what was being used back then, nothing beats quality research. Here’s the computer room which is basically a trip down the memory lane for the player (spot anything fancy?).

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7yyspaR.gif[/img]

Here we pay a short visit to the Torpedo Room where the explosion that ultimately sank Kursk happened. At 11:28 local time that explosion changed the crew’s routine practice maneuvers into a fight for survival.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/qajVJov.gif[/img]

Portraying Kursk in its damaged state raised a couple of visual and gameplay questions: What could withstand the initial explosion? Would fire spread dramatically? How long until the whole vessel would be flooded completely? What were the chances of reaching the emergency compartment? When working with realism these questions have to be answered and it all has to flow well with the gameplay.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/PftBYVE.gif[/img]

Throughout our entire development history KURSK was definitely the biggest project we’ve made and it took about 3.5 years to successfully complete it. We’ve been able to recreate the events from August 12, 2000 and KURSK became the first documentary adventure game that taught us many things about game development.  

[img]https://i.imgur.com/oJSiH7H.gif[/img]

Thank you for reading our Anniversary Post, it really means a lot to us! KURSK the game was released on November 7, 2018. Intrigued by the game? Launching the Anniversary Post also means we’ve got a [b]discount[/b] for anyone interested in trying the game out! 

Check out the game here: 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/860620/KURSK/

[h1][b]We salute the courage of the entire 118 personnel on board of the K-141! [/b][/h1] 

Follow us on our social media: [url=https://twitter.com/JujubeeGames]Twitter[/url], [url=https://www.facebook.com/Jujubee-267210603352542/]Facebook[/url],[url=https://www.instagram.com/jujubeegames/]Instagram[/url].

notes.title: Update 2.1.3 - Optimization!
notes.content:
Hello everyone,

We hope 2019 treats you well!

Today we've got an exciting update for you guys as we've managed to prepare a pretty solid patch which improves the optimization of the game, enabling a smoother experience. The framerate should be improved for people having low or medium settings set in the game.

Speaking of, we've improved the automatic detection of graphics settings - the system should now be more accurate of setting the best possible settings your PC can handle in order for you to have the best possible experience :)

Here's what this update brings in more detail:

[b]Added:[/b]
- some changes to how some sections load (all sections are now loaded from the start of the scene, no more loading between sections (with the exception of act 3 - we'll get there!))
- further optimization (especially on low and medium graphics settings)

[b]Fixes:[/b]
- automatic graphics settings detection is more accurate

NOTE: When you first start Kursk the system will automatically set the graphics settings for you, but you can always set them manually in the options menu :)

That's a pretty big update as it is something you guys have always wanted, so we're really glad that we we're able to turn up the framerate of our game. We hope that our streamers will be able to stream as long as they like without any frame drops.

Guys, if you happen to see a glitch or a bug, please do not hesitate to let us know! You can post a thread in the Steam discussions or contact us by e-mail: support@jujubee.pl.

We're not done yet! Still some awesome things are waiting to board the Kursk, so definitely stay in the neighbourhood for our future updates.

Let us know about the performance, it should be way more fun to explore the Kursk now :)

Until next time guys!

notes.title: The Explosion.
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hello there, everyone! [/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/c2b464c1d72fc40abd642ab031cb195516936be6.gif[/img]


The Kursk submarine disaster, the sinking of the Oscar-class submarine (Russian: Project 949A Антей Atomnaya Podvodnaya Lodka "Kursk" (APL "Kursk")) nuclear-powered submarine Kursk, took place during the first major Russian naval exercise in more than ten years, in the Barents Sea on 12 August 2000, killing all 118 personnel on board. Nearby ships registered the initial explosion and a second, much larger, explosion two minutes and fifteen seconds later, which was powerful enough to register on seismographs as far away as Alaska. The Russian Navy did not realise that the sub had sunk and did not halt the exercise or initiate a search for it for more than six hours. Because the sub's emergency rescue buoy had been intentionally disabled, it took more than 16 hours for them to locate the sunken boat.

While trying to complete your mission, you become witness to the dramatic events which shook the world at that time.

[h1][b] After the explosion: [/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/65c75fe4eb3b62fe5ec8313336e4c8d45af9b2f5.png[/img]

At 11:29:34 (07:29:50 UTC), seismic detectors at the Norwegian seismic array (NORSAR) and in other locations around the world recorded a seismic event of magnitude 1.5 on the Richter scale. The location was fixed at coordinates  WikiMiniAtlas69°38′N 37°19′E, North-East of Murmansk, approximately 250 kilometres (160 mi) from Norway, and 80 kilometres (50 mi) from the Kola Peninsula.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/90a6d597557b03fbcf5e0050e8be88e8e47cde71.png[/img]

[h1][b]Secondary event:[/b][/h1]

At 11:31:48, two minutes and 14 seconds after the first, a second event, measuring 4.2 on the Richter scale, or 250 times larger than the first, was registered on seismographs across Northern Europe and was detected as far away as Alaska. The second explosion was equivalent to 2–3 tons of TNT.

The seismic data showed that the explosion occurred at the same depth as the sea bed. The seismic event, triangulated at 69°36′N 37°34′E, showed that the boat had moved about 400 metres (1,300 ft) from the location of the initial explosion. It was enough time for the submarine to sink 108 metres (354 ft) and remain on the sea floor for a short while.

notes.title: The K-141 Submarine.
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hi there, everyone! [/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/c2b464c1d72fc40abd642ab031cb195516936be6.gif[/img]

Another Friday, so here is another one of our updates about the Game. 

[h1][b]HERE IS SOME INFORMATION ABOUT THE SUBMARINE: [/b][/h1]

K-141 Kursk was a Project 949A class Antey (Russian: Aнтей, meaning Antaeus) submarine of the Oscar-class, known as the Oscar II by its NATO reporting name, and was the penultimate submarine of the Oscar II class designed and approved in the Soviet Union. Construction began in 1990 at the Soviet Navy military shipyards in Severodvinsk, near Arkhangelsk, in the northern Russian SFSR. During the construction of K-141, the Soviet Union collapsed; work continued, and she became one of the first naval vessels completed after the collapse. K-141 was inherited by Russia and launched in 1994, before being commissioned by the Russian Navy on December 30, as part of the Russian Northern Fleet K-141 was named Kursk after the city, following the naming system for Soviet submarines.
Kursk was assigned to the home port of Vidyayevo, Murmansk Oblast.

[h1][b]HATCHES[/b][/h1]

notes.title: In the year 2000...
notes.content:
[h1][b]Hi there, everyone! [/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/c2b464c1d72fc40abd642ab031cb195516936be6.gif[/img]

The year 2000 was 18 (!) years ago, that’s such a long time, so many things have changed. 
Do you remember what the life was without smartphones, wearables, and all the technology we have today? 

As you know, our game takes place at the beginning of this millennium, and we wanted to keep the spirit of that time and try to capture many things you can probably recall from your very own memory. 

Like for example - In the Moscow Hotel, you will encounter some old-type electronics. 

[h1][b]ELECTRONICS[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/5a440d5486e9c73518a73cfc0ad35f60c8af8b23.gif[/img] 

Have you ever had a chance to work on those old, bulky, huge laptops many companies made? They weighed a lot, were really slow compared to the PCs we have today, not to mention their price.

[h1][b]PDA[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/b8e0bc476105c269d5d32c4808eeef6bf8e0a2e4.gif[/img]

Before the smartphone era began, there were some people who were using palmtops/PDAs (Personal Digital Assistant) - small computers (smaller than average laptop/netbook), they had many functions like calendar, notepad, even had an option to make photos or read some e-books! 

Player will have an opportunity to use our representation of the PDA (which will be his espionage equipment!), so you will have a chance to see what they looked like. 

[h1][b]Arcade Machines[/b][/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/82366df884a87f39d33abba99f989cf088dc086d.gif[/img]

This can take some of you way back! 
Have you had a chance to play on Arcade Machines?
 
Before everyone had the PCs at home, and before the whole “console wars” started, Video Arcades were the place where everyone was spending their money to play games. 
Did you know that on the board of the submarine there was actually an Arcade Machine?

This week we are focusing on the Vidyayevo: 

[h1][b]Trivia:[/b][/h1]

Vidyayevo (Russian: Видя́ево) is a closed rural inhabited locality in Murmansk Oblast, Russia. Despite having a rural status, it is municipally incorporated as Vidyayevo Urban Okrug, as such status is the only one allowed by the federal law for closed inhabited localities. The area has served as a base for diesel-powered submarines since the beginning of the 1960s. In 1979, it also became a base for nuclear-powered submarines. At Ara Bay, about a dozen nuclear-powered submarines are waiting for de-fueling and dismantlement. This facility also has small storage capacity for solid and liquid radioactive waste.

This is the place which was the home base for K-141 KURSK submarine, as well as for the other Akula, Sierra and Oscar-II (Antey) class submarines. 

The base at Ura Bay is used for diesel submarines and a few smaller surface vessels. The settlement consists mostly of five-story apartment buildings built on granite rock foundations or on poles driven into the permafrost.

[h1]Interactions! [/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/aa10945c103b025dc7896e8fafd6bfafcc1ff9aa.gif[/img]

Player will have an opportunity to use his PDA for lockpicking, as well as gather some intel before even getting on board of the submarine itself - try to check every location, and see for yourself what you can possibly find! 

[h1]Introduction! [/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/0c5951bf0ba545066e93a0f72723febcec8fdab3.gif[/img]

You will meet Wasilij - the Warrant Officer which will be your guardian, he will provide you with some small tasks before getting on board.

[h1]Base and the Submarine[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/47fc409070cac24529315472cc7ce68111e10221.gif[/img]

Player will be able to meet some of the crew members, and will be able to look around the naval base as there are some interesting quests involving this location.

notes.content:
Hi there, everyone! 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/03daa2db20d85b967946692872742d5645c3c0d3.gif[/img]

KURSK release is on 11th October 2018, and we are very excited to talk about the game. 
These posts will show up once a week - on Fridays until the day of the release.

Quick explanation what KURSK is really about:

[h1][b]SETTING:[/b][/h1]

You assume the role of a spy who finds his way on the Russian nuclear submarine K-141 Kursk. Your task is to collect secret information about the revolutionary Shkval supercavitating torpedoes. As you are trying to complete your mission, you become witness to the dramatic events which shook the world at that time.

KURSK is the first ever adventure and documentary video game inspired by real events.

[h1][b]ABOUT THE FEATURES: [/b][/h1]

[h1][b]LIVE THE HISTORY & THE WORLD OF 2000[/b][/h1]

You will experience the history of the fateful voyage of the K-141 Kursk submarine that ended at the bottom of the Barents Sea. During the game you will visit such places like a Hotel in Moscow where you will be briefed about your mission, or even the naval base in Vidyayevo, as well as the detailed inside of the submarine itself.

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/6ab471ce849db67429c8c13e36279977434949df.gif[/img]

[h1][b]ESPIONAGE/INTELLIGENCE OPERATIVE[/b][/h1]

As a spy, your mission is to collect information about the Shkval supercavitating torpedoes, which means that you’ll have an option to hack terminals, picklock restricted areas, and acquire intel about the submarine’s secrets. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33094842/aa10945c103b025dc7896e8fafd6bfafcc1ff9aa.gif[/img]

[h1][b]DECISIONS[/b][/h1]

Every decision you’ll make can have a long-lasting impact.
Get to know the crew of the Kursk submarine, make new friends, choose if you wish to help, or to ignore the task from person and see what happens!
